messages.author: 4fe26caaac11aa72
messages.subject: observed covariance matrix with FIML
parts:
Dear lavaan-users & authors,

is there a way to extract the "observed" cov-matrix when using the FIML-option?
That is, can I achieve the same results 1) using raw data an FIML, and 2) using a somehow adjusted cov-matrix?
I thought that 
inspect(fit.lc, "sampstat.h1")

would do the trick, but results differ.

Any advice is greatly appreciated.

Kind regards
Ulrich

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: observed covariance matrix with FIML
parts:
Ulrich,
I am not a statistician.  However, my understanding is as follows.
1. FIML directly maximizes the likelihood of the raw data.  It does not estimate a corrected moment matrix and then apply ML to that.
2. You could obtain the desired matrix by specifying your model as a free covariance matrix and estimating it using FIML.
3. I believe that the two procedures should produce comparable point estimates but the standard errors for the second procedure will not be incorrect because they will not reflect the uncertainty introduced by the missing data.

Graham, J. W. & Coffman, D. L. (2012).  Structural equation modeling with missing data.  In R. H. Hoyle (Ed.), Handbook of structural equation modeling (pp. 277-295).  New York:  Guilford Press.

Keith
------------------------
Keith A. Markus

http://jjcweb.jjay.cuny.edu/kmarkus

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: observed covariance matrix with FIML
parts: is there a way to extract the "observed" cov-matrix when using the FIML-option?

If you are looking for the ML estimate of the covariance matrix, yes you can get that from lavInspect(fit, "sampstat.h1").  That is the point estimate of the covariance matrix (the EM covariance matrix), as Keith said would be equivalent to fitting a saturated model to the partially observed data using FIML.  Fitting a hypothesized model to the EM covariance matrix would falsely assume complete data, so you could only trust the point estimates (not SEs or chi-squared).  However, adjustments have been worked out by Savalei & colleagues, which is implemented in the semTools package (the twostage() functions), although if you have nonnormal data, the scaled test statistic needs to be debugged.  

http://dx.doi.org/10.1080/10705510903008238

http://dx.doi.org/10.1080/10705511.2014.882692

Perhaps two-stage ML is not what you intend to do, since you are using FIML already.  Keith is right that FIML fits the hypothesized model directly to the available data, but lavaan does calculate the EM covariance matrix as part of the normal model fitting so that chi-squared can be calculated from the log-likelihood ratio comparing the saturated and hypothesized models.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
